Synopsis:
Lorroakan's initial dialog with the player in Ramazith's tower, where he plans to have Nightsong imprisoned like Ketheric had. He will ask the player to deliver her to him.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Lorroakan.json: You are meeting Lorroakan in Ramazith’s tower for the first time; he wants the Nightsong delivered to him so he can imprison it much like Ketheric did. Nightsong is a powerful relic/being the party will already know about—Lorroakan even has a binding circle prepared that mirrors the one Ketheric used in Act 2. He rejects service to gods, claims a goal of “equalising man and god” (seeking longevity or immortality), and promises to reward anyone who aids him. Off‑screen this frames a clear choice: the player is being asked to hand Nightsong over into Lorroakan’s custody rather than keep or protect it.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_LorroakanConclusion.json: Lorroakan's dialoge after winning the fight against Nightsong. In gameplay he will attempt to fit her into the soul cage device (after this dialogue-- this should remain bronze).
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_FinalConfrontation.json: Nightsong's confrontation with Lorroakan in his tower, once the player tells Nightsong (or she finds out) that Lorroakan is looking for her.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Rolan.json: Dialog with Sorcerous Sundries' clerk Rolan. He will explain how Lorroakan is neglecting him in his search for the Nightsong. Player can ask Rolan to make a portal to Lorroakan.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Aradin.json: Aradin is parked in front of the Sorcerous Sundries, shouting at Klank (the construct blocking the shop entrance) and making a public scene. Off‑screen he was hired by Lorroakan, the wizard owner, to recover the "Nightsong" and led men into a goblin hive—he suffered casualties and now blames Lorroakan for sending him after what he thought was a relic. The player has already been involved with the Nightsong quest (one possible outcome being they found the Nightsong and discovered it is actually an aasimar), so Aradin turns to the player to ask whether they had any success and to demand Lorroakan pay up. He’s agitated and threatening, but ultimately leaves after pressing the point.

context: You are meeting Lorroakan for the first time in Ramazith’s tower; he wants the Nightsong delivered to him and even has a binding circle prepared that mirrors the one Ketheric used in Act 2. Nightsong is a powerful relic/being the party already knows about (in some playthroughs the player has discovered it is actually an aasimar), and Lorroakan intends to imprison it to further his stated goal of “equalising man and god” — he rejects service to gods and seeks longevity or immortality. He promises rewards to anyone who helps, so the scene frames a clear choice: hand Nightsong over to Lorroakan or keep/protect her. Off‑screen his pursuit has already affected others (he’s sent agents and neglected associates like Rolan, and antagonised Aradin), which may factor into later reactions and confrontations.
